chunks: He said: Abu Amru Uthman ibn Ahmad al-Daqqaq permitted me to report, he said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik reported to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Awdi narrated to us, he said: Mukhawwal ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from al-Rabee' ibn al-Mundhir, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn Ali, peace be upon them both, who said:
"There is no servant whose eyes shed a drop for us, or whose eyes fill with tears for us, except that Allah will grant him a place in Paradise for ages."

Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Awdi said: Then I saw al-Husayn ibn Ali, peace be upon them both, in a dream, and I said: "Mukhawwal ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, from al-Rabee' ibn al-Mundhir, from his father, from you, that you said: 'There is no servant whose eyes shed a drop for us, or whose eyes fill with tears for us, except that Allah will grant him a place in Paradise for ages.'" He said: "Yes." I said: "The chain of narration between me and you has fallen away."
seo_question: What is the reward for crying over Imam Husayn and the Ahlulbayt?
Did any narrator receive direct confirmation from Imam Husayn in a dream?
ai.summary: Imam al-Husayn ibn Ali (AS) declares that any servant of God who sheds even a single tear or whose eyes fill with tears out of grief for the Ahlulbayt will be guaranteed a place in Paradise for ages. The narrator Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Awdi then recounts seeing Imam al-Husayn in a dream, repeating the hadith back to him, and receiving direct confirmation. He joyfully realizes that the chain of narration between himself and the Imam has dissolved, since he heard it directly from the Imam in the dream. This teaching, delivered in the context of mourning for the Ahlulbayt, powerfully affirms the spiritual merit of grief and weeping for the Prophet's family, a cornerstone practice of Shia devotion particularly associated with the tragedy of Karbala.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 6. He said: Abu Amru Uthman ibn Ahmd al-Daqqaq permitted me to report what he reported from Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik, who reported from Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Awadi, who reported from Mukhawwal Ibn Ibrahim, from al-Rabee’ ibn al-Munzir, from his father who reported from: Al-Husayn ibn ‘Ali, peace be upon him, that he said:
"Whoever sheds a tear from his eyes for us, or fills his eyes with tears for us, Allah will grant him for that an eternal place in Paradise."

Ahmed ibn Yahya al-Awadi said: I saw al-Husayn ibn ‘Ali, peace be upon him, in dream and related to him: "Mukhawwal ibn Ibrahim has reported to me from al-Rabee’ ibn al-Munzir, from his father from you that you said: Whoever sheds a tear from his eyes for us, or fills his eyes with tears for us, Allah will grant him an eternal place in Paradise." He said: "Yes." So I said: "(In that case), the chain of narration between you and me does not exist any more."
